title: 2026 CMA Awards Kicks Off With Emotional Tribute to Dolly Parton: ‘Our Tennessee Angel Is With the Angels’
summary: Host Lainey Wilson and Vince Gill began the show by singing the late country icon's hit.
contentText:
Country music — and indeed, the world — will always love Dolly Parton . And to kick off the 2026 CMA Awards held at the Bridgestone Arena in Nashville on Wednesday (Nov. 18), the ceremony began by paying tribute to the iconic singer, who died at age 80 on Aug. 25

“Dolly gave us hope. Dolly gave us joy. Dolly gave us heart,” host Lainey Wilson began at the top of the show before reminding viewers of one of the late star’s lessons: “We are all God’s children who should always be there for one another. Now our Tennessee angel is with the angels. … We will always love you.”

The cameras then panned over to where Vince Gill was standing as the opening strains of “I Will Always Love You,” which Parton penned in the early 1970s, a song that Whitney Houston took to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1992. The “Feels Like Love” crooner — who alongside Parton released a duet of the track in 1995 — began the tribute on his own, with Wilson later joining him to trade verses as a black-and-white photo of a smiling Parton glowed behind them.

As the pair sang, the cameras panned to the audience to show Taylor Swift singing along from the audience, as did Luke Combs and other country stars. The duet ended to a standing ovation.

The show was hosted for a third straight year by Wilson. Going into the evening, Ella Langley, who exploded this year with the popularity of her Hot 100 record-setting hit “Choosin’ Texas,” led in nominations with an impressive nine nods. Miranda Lambert was close behind with seven, while Kacey Musgraves and Ben West were next with five a piece.

The 2026 CMA Awards aired live on ABC and Disney+, and streams on Hulu the following day.
